To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
insulin degradation in lysosomes is a two step process, the first step is a transhydrogenation of insulin to a reduced form, the second step is a proteolytic cleavage.
insulin degradation by lysosomal enzymes is a major route for insulin inactivation.
the lysosomes of the liver contain both the glutathione-insulins transhydrogenase (GTI) and the “insulin specific” protease.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the degradation of insulin by lysosomal enzymes, and the results indicate that lysosomes may be a site of hormone degradation.
the degradation of insulin by lysosomal extracts.
the mechanism of insulin degradation by lysosomes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
insulin is first bound to its specific plasma membrane receptor, then endocytosis of the hormone-receptor complex occurs.
insulin binds to receptors on the plasma membrane, is then internalized, degraded in lysosomes, and the resulting amino acids are recycled for use in protein synthesis.
lysosomes play an important role in the intracellular degradation of insulin and possibly also of other hormones.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the lysosomal enzymes, glutathione-insulins transhydrogenase (EC 1.8.4.2), and “insulin protease”, which are normally present in the cytosolic fraction, can be found in the lysosomes of rat liver.
insulin binds to the plasma membrane, is internalized, and then degraded by lysosomal enzymes.
lysosomal extracts from liver contain both insulin specific protease and glutathione-insin transhydrogenase, and that the latter enzyme can be shown to be a glutathione-inslin transpeptidase.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the lysosome is a very active degradative organelle, and the presence of insulin degrading enzymes within the lysosome suggests that lysosomal degradation may be a major pathway for insulin degradation.
insulin is degraded in lysosomes.
the insulin receptor is not the only way that insulin can enter the cell.
